title: Envelope constraints from NB-06 in the engine: the street-wall (ZR 35-631(b)/23-431(b)), setback-above-base (23-432/23-433, 35-632(a)) and side-yard (23-335(b)/34-232) checks in a new scenario/three_answers/envelope_constraints.py with three states (applies->Conditional; not_applicable; not_known), per-frontage wide/narrow via the accepted D-052 classifier, 1.5.0 envelope_rows + constraint_lines (street_wall_band/setback_line not_established on the benchmark) + input_facts emission threaded through the live route, page-6 and page-8 made to agree with page-3 on every document version, the G-5 benchmark regenerated, three new rule files + the review register, and NB-06 rev 3 (closing condition 3 with the now-present 12-10 captures). NB-05 code identity; NB-01 contingency.
objective: Carry NB-06 into the scenario engine and the report as labelled Conditional drafts, behaviour-identical on 1.4.0. (1) New scenario/three_answers/envelope_constraints.py (mirror rear_yard_checks.py): build_envelope_analysis(...) -> EnvelopeAnalysis(envelope_rows, constraint_lines, input_facts) holding the three checks, each with state applies/not_applicable/not_known and its conditions, text and zr_sections. STREET WALL (ZR 35-631(b) via 34-11->34-24(b)(1)->35-63 for residential-only and 35-01->35-63 for mixed; 23-431(b) when no overlay): applies, 8 ft of the street line on each frontage, Conditional on the prevailing-frontage test and the operative street line; plain R6B without the overlay is 8 ft wide / 10 ft narrow (the D-051 asymmetry, never collapsed). SETBACK (23-432 table R6B 30/45/55 -> 23-433; 35-632(a)): keyed on building street-wall height vs the 45 ft maximum base height; <=45 not triggered, >45 ft 10 ft (wide)/15 ft (narrow); unknown width withholds (D-051, never narrow by default); 23-433(a)-(d) modifications carried. SIDE YARD (23-335(b); 34-232 in the overlay): none required, 5 ft minimum for an open area if provided; single/two-family detached is 23-335(a) two 5-ft yards without the overlay, removed by 34-232 with it. (2) Per-frontage wide/narrow by REUSING app.spatial.frontage_street_width.derive_frontage_street_widths + app.connectors.dcm_street_width_policy (D-052; never reinvented), from StreetData threaded by M5-T167. (3) Emit the 1.5.0 envelope_rows, the constraint_lines (both street_wall_band and setback_line not_established on the benchmark: the operative street line is not fixed by a mapped width - D-094-R017, NB-06 condition, DB-260) and the input_facts, via a thin _apply_envelope in three_way_document.py and the existing conditional version-bump; a new _envelope_analysis_for in result_way_engine_bridge.py threaded into the evidence/route emit only (mirror _rear_yard_analysis_for, never the legacy adapter). (4) result_ways.py _setback_way moves from Withheld to agree, byte-for-meaning, with envelope_rows[setback] (lesson iii); result_way_inputs.py gains any needed input state. (5) first_option_results.py gates 'The street wall' out of _NOT_CHECKED_BASE ONLY when the engine applied the check, so pages 3, 6 and 8 agree on every document (1.4.0 byte-identical). (6) readers.py (page-8 appendix) shows the applied conditional street-wall/setback/side-yard result from the document's own 1.5.0 blocks (new _apply_street_wall_open_item / _apply_setback_open_item mirroring M5-T167's _apply_rear_yard_open_item), byte-identical to today on a 1.4.0 document - SEE RISK 1. (7) Three new rule files r6b_street_wall / r6b_setback / r6b_side_yard (names/families fixed at G0; mirror r6b_rear_yard_corner_waiver.rule.json) and the review register (G-11, no human verdict). (8) Regenerate the whole G-5 benchmark set from the corrected engine (never hand-edited): the recorded journey gains envelope_rows/constraint_lines/input_facts; update every pinning consumer only where the engine output moved. (9) NB-06 rev 3 adds the 23-433(a)-(d) modifications and, with an independent reading of the now-present 12-10 street-wide/street-narrow captures, closes condition 3; NB-05 code-identity revision and the NB-01 contingency both fire (result_way_bridge.py/result_ways.py/three_way_document.py are in their code_paths). Expected values come ONLY from NB-06, overlay-reading.json/real-lot.json and the law, never a program run; the benchmark results stay Conditional, never an unconditional 'complies'.
business_reason: D-094 R017/R043/R061/R082 and the owner's 2026-10-14 review: page 5/6 still omit the street-wall, setback and side-yard envelope constraints; the next milestone (R143) is a scenario placed on the actual site with reconciled calculations and clearly identified remaining constraints. The law is known for these three checks - they must not read 'not checked' only because the feature was unfinished (R061) - while the genuinely unresolved site facts (operative street line, prevailing frontage, building type) stay unresolved.

risks: RISK 1 (top, neither candidate plan caught it): readers.py builds page-8 appendix open items with 'setback' and 'street_wall' categories. When the engine applies the checks they will DROP from page 8 (the Withheld way and the not-checked line both clear) while page 3 shows the applied reading - unless readers.py gains _apply_street_wall_open_item / _apply_setback_open_item mirroring M5-T167's _apply_rear_yard_open_item. The work order forbids readers.py; this packet OVERRIDES that forbid (readers.py in allowed_paths) for page-3/6/8 parity (R136 class). If G0 instead decides the items may simply drop, readers.py stays forbidden but the real-print check (S10) must prove page 8 does not contradict page 3 and the conditions still appear. Resolve at G0 before the build; do not discover it at the gate as M5-T167 did.
RISK 2: result_ways.py _setback_way is a second setback emitter; it must agree byte-for-meaning with envelope_rows[setback] (lesson iii). Plan B omitted result_ways.py - do not drop it from scope.

RISK 3: setback row STATE for the 30 ft option (not_applicable vs applies+conditions) is a G1 legal-reading decision, not a code choice; worked from NB-06 Q2 + overlay-reading first. Tests cover both <=45 and >45 behaviour regardless of the label.

RISK 4: three_way_document.py (warn band) and result_ways.py must not cross JUSTIFY (750); keep _apply_envelope thin or carry it in envelope_constraints.py. NB-05 (rev 4) and NB-01 (rev 5) list these files in code_paths - the code-identity revisions and the NB-01 contingency delta review are in scope.
RISK 5: benchmark fan-out (M5-T167 lesson i) - the enumerated consumer tests, the DXF/SVG snapshots and the web pins must all be in allowed_paths up front; a missed pin costs a scope correction.

RISK 6 (sequencing): M5-T180 (the DB-245 wording sweep split off from M5-T167) also regenerates the one benchmark and touches result_way_bridge.py/result_ways.py. M5-T170 and M5-T180 must run serially (one owner of the benchmark at a time), never in parallel. M5-T169 (next) reads readers.py after M5-T170 lands.

RISK 7: thread the envelope analysis ONLY into the evidence/route emit (run_engine_and_result_ways_from_evidence), never the legacy adapter at :247; the live route carries street_data only after M5-T167 is accepted.

RISK 8 (pre-check A-1): results.schema.json envelope_value.value is a number: emit the setback depths as two numeric values (10 wide, 15 narrow, unit ft) with their frontage, never NB-06's basis string '10 (wide) / 15 (narrow)'.

RISK 9 (DB-266, found by the orchestrator in the print of main 2bcdb05a on 2026-10-15): M5-T175's _constraint_rows_from_results skips a kind with no envelope row, so the first 1.5.0 document with a rear_yard block (M5-T167) lost the setback and street-wall rows on page 3 while page 8 kept them; the reviews of M5-T167 compared pages 6 and 8 only. Fixed here (scenario on page 3 fallback) and checked on the real print.

RISK 10 (side yard of a mixed building): two sealed readers disagreed; a research helper read the official text (session-2026-10-15a/return-research-mixed-side-yard.md): not required, Conditional on the 5-ft open-area minimum, via ZR 35-01 -> 35-21 -> 35-22 -> 23-335(b); 34-232 by its words reaches a 'residential building' only; 35-24 is not captured and is not cited. G1 compares the engine with the two sealed readings (kept from the builder) and that research.
